core_meaning.short_meaning: Generous and cheerful; companion Bujayr ibn Zuhayr.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Bujayr (بُجَيْر) is an authentic Arabic masculine given name meaning 'broadhearted', 'generous in spirit', or 'prosperous and cheerful'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Bujayr ibn Zuhayr al-Muzani, an early convert who fought at Hunayn and Ta'if, whose poetic letter to his brother Ka'b ibn Zuhayr led to Ka'b's famous conversion and the recitation of the prophetic praise poem Banat Su'ad.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive form of abjar, expressing affectionate broadness of chest, magnanimity, and rich hospitality.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Bujayr was the son of the great pre-Islamic poet Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma. He traveled to Medina and embraced Islam enthusiastically. When his brother Ka'b composed verses mocking his conversion, Bujayr wrote back urging him with heartfelt brotherly wisdom to abandon False gods and seek the forgiveness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His letter transformed Ka'b's heart, leading to his journey to Medina and the presentation of the Prophet's mantle (Burdah).
